scope: Target candidates of the catalog this was built against; one row each.

olfactory_bulk.citation: Olender T, et al. The human olfactory transcriptome. BMC Genomics 2016;17:619.
olfactory_bulk.table: Table S2, columns OE7, OE12, OE15, OE17 (olfactory mucosa) and respiratory (one nasal respiratory sample); FPKM

cells.source: CELLxGENE Census 2025-11-08, primary normal tissue, adult, UMI protocols

grades.note: A tissue is recorded only at grade medium or high. FPKM and single-cell counts per million are read on the nTPM scale as an approximation.

limits: Olfactory biopsies mix olfactory and respiratory epithelium. The table is from 2016 gene symbols; proteins without a matching symbol are unmeasured, not absent.
One nasal respiratory bulk sample exists. Its value is reported and never recorded on its own.
Census nasal cells are brushings of respiratory epithelium. They hold no olfactory neurons.

Scalp and tongue have one dataset each, so nothing is recorded from them. The scalp cells are follicular keratinocytes, not hair-shaft cortex, where hair keratins and keratin-associated proteins are made.
One skin dataset (e7c5ba7e) shows many testis genes at similar rates in every cell type. Requiring two datasets keeps that from recording a tissue.
Melanocytes are left out by request, as are cells without a type.
